newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway Aker RGI profits up on asset sale.
newsitem.headline: Norway Aker RGI profits up on asset sale.

text.p: Norwegian industrial holding group Aker RGI ASA said on Tuesday first-quarter net profits quadrupled to 210 million crowns ($29.4 million) thanks to the sale of assets.
Turnover rose to 6.06 billion crowns from 4.55 billion, operating profits dropped to 158 million from 271 million while pre-tax profits rose to 374 million from 166 million crowns.
In March, Aker RGI sold 35 percent of the shares it held in real estate group Avantor ASA. This yielded a gain of 335 million crowns to help increase profits.

"Active efforts have been made by Norway's Aker RGI group since its establishment to concentrate operations on a smaller range of equity holdings. Over the first four months, the group has sold assets worth more than three billion NOK," it said.

The comparative 1996 figures were calculated on a pro forma basis following the establishment of the conglomerate last year from the merger of engineering and construction company AKER ASA and investment group RGI ASA.

The group's core business areas are Nordic cement and building materials group Scancem, fishing and fish processing company Norway Seafoods -- the world's largest operator for catching and processing white fish -- and the offshore services firm Aker Maritime.

Scancem, in which Aker RGI holds 33.3 percent, saw operating losses swing further into the red to 82 million Swedish crowns from 47 million. The losses were blamed on weaker results from the Nordic cement and concrete products business areas, which were hit by a slump in the Swedish market.
Norway Seafoods' operating profits fell to 104 million NOK from 108 million NOK, but the division expected profits to rise significantly this year compared with 1996.
Norway Seafoods, which is 54.7 percent owned by Aker RGI, expects its shares to be quoted on the Oslo Stock Exchange sometime this month.
Aker Maritime, in which the holding group controls 75.1 percent, reported operating profits rising to 72 million NOK from 65 million.

"Improved results for Aker Maritime were influenced in particular by better performances in the United States, Britain, the product companies and the subsidiaries specialising in operations support, maintenance and modifications on the Norwegian continental shelf," the company said.
